about: nxsuite inventory: the 147 hardware claims (spec v1) and the test table that answers them. Read by tools/hwtests/nxsuite_gen.py (the .nex test table) and tools/hwtests/intake.py. GPL-3.0-or-later, part of nexclash.

tests.title: $08 bit 6 latch
tests.fields: 8 samples (lines 20-27, the write at the start of the line): T from the NEXTREG $08 write to the first read (reads 23 T apart) that shows the new bit 6; v = max, min, t0 = how many were 0. Board run 5: v=23 min=0 t0=2 - the new bit is read back by the first or the second read every time (two populations = which side of the change the first read lands): the read-back follows the write within 23 T, it does not keep the old bit until dot 256 of the line.

tests.title: line interrupt position
tests.fields: pN = T at 3.5 MHz from the line interrupt for line N to the moment the raster counter ($1E / $1F) reads N (negative = before), mean of 5; sN = spread of the 5 raw readings (above ~24 T = not repeatable). Board run 5: mid-frame p100=-150 s100=0 and p191=-149 s191=2 - the interrupt comes 150 T (+-12) before the counter reads N, i.e. 78 T after the counter read N-1 (a 228 T line), repeatable; near the frame end it moves and spreads (p0=-7 s0=88, plast2=-122 s50): those two lines sit next to the counter's wrap at the frame end, where this test's own sync waits cross the frame boundary - read them as 'not constant there', not as a position.

tests.title: one outstanding CTC
tests.fields: v = the most handler runs in one interrupts-on window after 5 CTC0 wraps with interrupts off (1 = the requests folded into one, 2-5 = they queued); least = the fewest; runs / periods = the old busy-handler ratio (board runs 4 / 5: 0.24-0.25), which cannot decide fold against queue.

tests.title: DMA yields to HW IM2
tests.fields: v = bytes the DMA had copied when the handler ran; line = where; bad = wrong bytes after the EI run; dbad = wrong bytes after the interrupts-off run; pend = requests already waiting before the start (taken first); di = completes / returned-not-copied / paused-at-request. Board run 5: 1212 bytes at line 248, bad=0; dbad=15203 = 1181 bytes copied: with interrupts off the DMA stops at the ULA request at the same place and, with no acknowledge, does not restart - the CPU runs on (no hang).

tests.title: 50 / 60 Hz table
tests.fields: The same numbers at both rates ($05 bit 2 switched and put back): l50 / l60 lines per frame, t50 / t60 line length in T (3.5 MHz), i50 / i60 the raster line at which the ULA interrupt status ($C8 bit 0) was first seen. v = l60. The intake prints them side by side.

tests.title: copper line vs raster
tests.fields: lL = the line read after the copper's MOVE showed; oL = T (3.5 MHz) from the raster counter change to the MOVE's effect (negative = the MOVE first), median of 3 frames; sL = spread. Board runs 4 and 5: o191 = -62 / -60 with s191 = 0 and 0 at lines 0, 120, 250: a WAIT for line 191 - the last display line - takes effect about 60 T (a quarter line) before the counter reads 191, every frame; the other lines coincide within the poll step. The copper line number still equals the counter (l191 = 191).

tests.title: DMA cost per byte
tests.fields: keys <m|p><a|3|2><35|28> = clocks of 28 MHz per byte (memory / port $5B; timing byte absent / 3 / 2; 3.5 / 28 MHz), slope (t2048 - t256) / 1792. Board run 5 (d99fbf8): 0 / 584 / 0.32 were a timing fault - in continuous mode the CPU is frozen and the CTC3 wraps were lost; the board's own nb.DMA rows predict about 4.99 clocks (28 MHz) and 32 (3.5 MHz) at timing byte 2. method=fault marks a slope outside 0.5-100 (INFO, never FAIL).

tests.title: DMA prescaler
tests.fields: pP_<35|28> = clocks of 28 MHz per byte in burst mode with prescaler P. Board run 5 (d99fbf8): 16 for every P was a test fault (the tick count was overwritten before use); JNext after the fix: about 32 x P (875 kHz / P).

tests.title: burst CPU share
tests.fields: v = the CPU's polling-loop rate during a burst (P = 100) against the same loop with no DMA, %; cont = the same during a continuous transfer. Board run 5 (d99fbf8): 104 % came from comparing loop counts over different lengths; rates are compared now.

tests.title: blitter cost
tests.left_out: The 32-ball figure is a workload, not one register behaviour. Its parts are measured: D13 clocks per byte of opaque / transparent copies and fill, D12 the 2D copies, G7 N01 the LDIR and DMA rows; drawing the figure's 320 x 256 scene and timing it per frame would add a picture, not a new hardware answer.

tests.title: DMA set-up costs
tests.left_out: Measured by G7 N01, per call at 3.5 and 28 MHz: the nb.DMA, nb.DMA_rtg, nb.DMA_rrun and nb.DMA_brst rows and the suite-only rows nb.DMA_cont.1 ($D3 continue, $87) and nb.DMA_arm.256 (WR0 port A only $1D, $CF, $87); a second copy of the same rows here would add nothing.

tests.title: collision rules
tests.fields: side = two opaque dots side by side (0 = no collision), same = on the same dot (1), clip = an overlap outside the clip window (1 = still collides), off = with $15 bit 0 = 0 (1 = still collides), second = a second $303B read (0 = the first read cleared it), alone = control, one sprite by itself (must be 0). Board run 5 (KS1 3.03.00): 0 1 1 1 0 0 = the claim exactly.

tests.title: accidental relative
tests.fields: x160 = a probe at the anchor X + byte 0 (relative place), x10 = a probe at byte 0 alone (absolute place); 1 = it collided. Board run 5: x160=1 x10=0 = relative (byte 4 bits 7:6 = 01 makes an 8-bit sprite relative).

tests.title: sprites per line
tests.fields: v = the smallest number k of unscaled sprites on one line that sets $303B bit 1 (k-1 fit); s2 / s4 / s8 = the same at X scale 2 / 4 / 8; moved = with all 128 shown, how many must leave the line to clear the flag. Board run 5: 106 / moved 23 (105 fit whether the other 23 are hidden or shown on another line): fits 17 clocks a sprite in a 1,785-1,801 clock budget (the claim's 1,792 for 48K), not 18 in 1,824. s2-s8 = 60 there only meant 'below 60' (the sweep started at 60; it now starts at 1).

tests.title: $64 = 32 / 33 L2 top
tests.fields: V18: o33 / o32 = the answer with $64 = 33, then 32: two (Layer 2 row 0 turned white by the copper at its line 0, plus the reference row 4) or one (only the reference). means=<o33>-<o32>; the claim: two-one. JNext 1.3.0 lights row 0 with $64 = 32 and not with 33 (one-two): an emulator answer only.

tests.title: per machine timing
tests.fields: Per timing t = 1 48K, 2 128K, 3 +3, 4 Pentagon: l<t> = lines per frame, i<t> = the raster line at which NextReg $C8 bit 0 (ULA interrupt status) was first seen (polled at 28 MHz, no interrupt taken), r<t> = $03 read back; v = how many l<t> are the claims' frame lengths (VGA 312 / 311 / 311 / 320). Builds up to e8cc11b also wrote out=vga/hdmi from $11: no source says $11 shows the output (board run 7: HDMI cable, $11 = $00); ignore it - the header geom= and the V19 cable answer say which frame was measured. JNext: 312/311/311/320, i 248/248/248/239.

tests.title: timing change frame end
tests.fields: $03 written at line 100 of a frame: v = that frame's length (counted from line 100 to its fall), j1 = the line read just after the fall, f2 / f3 the next frames, exp0 / exp1 the old and new lengths. v = exp0 and f2 = exp1: taken at the frame end (the claim). JNext gives v = 247, j1 = 239 (the counter jumped at once): an emulator answer only.

tests.title: contention per timing
tests.fields: c<t> = extra raster lines (1024 reads of the bank from $C000 at 3.5 MHz, against bank 0) for banks 1,3,4,5,7; one line = 228 T, so 1 line ~ 0.22 T a read; lim = 3 lines = contended. nr08 = $08 at the start (bit 6 written 0 for the test, put back). v = book when 128K = 1 3 5 7, +3 = 4 5 7, Pentagon = none.

tests.title: 48K timing 7FFD
tests.fields: 48K timing: a6 / a7 = MMU 6 / 7 after OUT $7FFD,$13, b6 / b7 after OUT $3FFD,$13 ($FF $FF: not written, NextReg $D8 bit 0 set at launch = the +3 disk ports trapped); nrd8 = $D8 at launch. PASS if both gave 6 / 7. p3ffd=skipped: NextReg $D8 bit 0 was set at launch (the +3 disk ports trapped), so $3FFD was not written and b6 / b7 = $FF mean nothing (board run 7: nrd8=$01).

tests.title: 128K timing 1FFD
tests.fields: 128K timing: r0-r3 = CRC of $0000-$3FFF for ($1FFD bit 2, $7FFD bit 4) = 00, 01, 10, 11; s04 = S04's CRC of ROM 3 at the start. PASS if r3 = s04 and the four differ.

tests.title: restore timing
tests.fields: v = lines per frame after $03 is written with the start timing; exp = the preamble's; nr03 / start03 = $03 now / at the start. PASS if both agree; the progress record's timing flag is cleared.

tests.title: $BB bit 6
tests.fields: nrbb = $BB at the start; mapped1 = DivMMC still over $0000 after one F_OPEN (read, no such file) with bit 6 flipped; mapped2 = after one more with $BB put back; opened = the file existed (1). v = set-enables / set-disables (which bit value stopped the exit) or no-change.

tests.title: $3Dxx instant automap
tests.fields: a = A after CALL $3D00 with LD A,$3D : RET in the alt ROM and automap on; $3D = the ROM image ran (no instant automap, FAIL), else DivMMC memory ran (PASS); mapped = DivMMC still over $0000 after one F_OPEN.

tests.title: RST 38 trap
tests.fields: v = A after RST $38 with SCF : LD A,$5A : RET in the alt ROM and automap on; cy = carry; $5A = no trap (FAIL), else the DivMMC trap took over after $0038 (PASS); mapped as XD2.

tests.title: auto-restart freeze
tests.fields: v = main-loop passes between $87 and the stop (the CPU had the bus that often); irq = handler runs (the handler stops the DMA at the second); bad = bytes of the 256-byte copy that differ. PASS if stopped and v <= 50. A machine that does not come back = the escape (hardware IM2 + $CC) failed: HANG-GUARD. JNext 1.3.0 hangs here (no $CC escape); CSpect PASS v=1. The DMA must answer one byte first: a DMA still locked by an earlier XH2 gives SKIP why=dma-deaf (board run 7 pass 2 printed FAIL v=15812 bad=254 that way).

tests.title: WR4 interrupt lock
tests.fields: XH2: first pass: one DMA byte; if it does not arrive the DMA is already deaf: SKIP why=dma-deaf (nothing sent). Else before / after = 1-byte copies before and after the WR4 byte $91 (bit 4); v = deaf (PASS) or copied (FAIL). Then power off and on (or a hard reset), start again, H: a 1 / 2 / 3 question gives reset=soft / hard / power and v = reset-frees or still-locked (the start's DMA byte, PRG_XH2), OPERATOR. The verdict uses the lock pass; the note states each follow-up. Board run 7 (KS1, 3.03.00): pass 4 ran in the same run as the lock (no restart) and found the DMA still deaf; the files hold no start after a reset, so what F4 does is not yet shown.

claims.claim: A .nex started from NextZXOS can create and write a file on the SD card through esxDOS RST 8 (F_OPEN $9A, F_WRITE $9E, F_CLOSE $9B) with MMU slots 0/1 = $FF, interrupts off and a stack outside slots 0/1.
